gameSystem.name: Night Job
gameSystem.description: A game for use with Cyberpunk RED, for players new to solo play, with two guided flows: a heist one-shot for one evening of work, and a campaign in three acts where a small crew makes a name. Original content: flows, clocks, rep and heat, a survival economy and tables.

tags.label: Client
tags.hint: The one paying for the job

tags.label: Fixer
tags.hint: Brings you work and takes a cut

tags.label: Netrunner
tags.hint: Owns the net side of a job

trackers.name: Alarm
trackers.hint: At 6/6 security locks down and you run

trackers.name: Edge
trackers.hint: A spare advantage you can spend to dodge trouble

trackers.name: Rep
trackers.hint: What the street says about your crew

trackers.name: Heat
trackers.hint: At 8+ someone sends a hit squad

trackers.name: Lifestyle
trackers.hint: What you eat, month after month

trackers.name: Housing
trackers.hint: Where you sleep, and what it costs

trackers.name: On a gig
trackers.hint: 1 while a gig runs: the street waits. Set it to 0 if you drop the gig.

sceneTypes.name: Social
sceneTypes.purpose: Talk, bargain or bluff with someone.
sceneTypes.tips: Decide what you want from the other person before you ask. Use the Fate question when you do not know how they react, and play the dice for the hard parts with your Cyberpunk RED rules (see the Cyberpunk RED core rulebook, Skills chapter).

play.title: Who do you talk to, and what do you want?
play.tip: Name them with the Street names table if you have no one in mind.

play.title: Do they give you what you ask?
play.tip: Ask for something fair as 50/50, something steep as unlikely.

sceneTypes.name: Exploration
sceneTypes.purpose: Look around a place and see what is there.
sceneTypes.tips: Scout the job site: entrances, guards, cameras. One good detail is worth more than a long list. Anything you learn can help you in the heist.

play.title: Do you find a way in?
play.tip: A yes is a lead, not a free pass.

sceneTypes.name: Crew
sceneTypes.purpose: Put the crew together.
sceneTypes.tips: A crew of two to four is plenty. Give each person a role and a street name, and say what they are good at. Start with your own character.

setup.title: Who are you?
setup.tip: Make your character: a street name, a role, a few stats and your kit. You can edit the sheet any time in the Characters panel.

setup.title: Who is your first crew member?
setup.tip: Someone you trust with your back. Just a street name: it becomes the NPC's name. Write what they are good at in a note.

setup.title: Who else is in?
setup.tip: Just a street name: it becomes the NPC's name. Write what they are good at in a note.

setup.title: Who drives?
setup.tip: Skip it if nobody on the crew can drive: you will take the wheel yourself. Otherwise, just a street name: it becomes the NPC's name.

sceneTypes.name: Briefing
sceneTypes.purpose: Meet the client and hear the job.
sceneTypes.tips: Roll the tables to get the job, then make it yours. The facts you fill appear in the Facts panel, and the payout comes back at the end.

setup.title: Who is the client?
setup.tip: Roll for a client. Not a fit? Use Refill in the Facts panel.

setup.title: What's the plan?
setup.tip: One sentence: how you get in, and how you get out.

setup.title: What's the catch?
setup.tip: Every job has a catch the client left out. Decide it now or leave it for later.

sceneTypes.name: Netrun
sceneTypes.purpose: Jack in and work the net architecture.
sceneTypes.tips: Go down one floor at a time and roll what waits on each. Run the details with your Cyberpunk RED rules (see the Cyberpunk RED core rulebook, Netrunning chapter). Keep it short: a few floors tell the story.

play.title: Which Black ICE is it?
play.tip: Only when the floor holds Black ICE.

play.title: What do you do here, and how does it go?

sceneTypes.name: Infiltration
sceneTypes.purpose: Get inside unseen.
sceneTypes.tips: Move quietly and describe one obstacle at a time. A failed attempt raises the alarm. A very bad one blows your cover and turns the scene into a firefight.

play.title: How do you try to get in?
Do you slip past?
play.tip: Roll Hands against a difficulty that grows with the alarm. A fail raises the alarm by one. A botch starts a firefight.

sceneTypes.name: Firefight
sceneTypes.purpose: Shoot your way through.
sceneTypes.tips: Keep it short and loud. Run the shooting with your Cyberpunk RED rules (see the Cyberpunk RED core rulebook, Combat chapter) and use this scene only to learn who comes for you and how it ends.

sceneTypes.name: Grab
sceneTypes.purpose: Take what you came for.
sceneTypes.tips: This is the moment of the job. Describe how you reach the target, then say if you got it. Getting it ends the heist and starts the escape.

play.title: How do you get to the target?

closing.title: Got it?
closing.tip: Choose Yes when the target is in your hands. The heist phase ends.

sceneTypes.name: Getaway
sceneTypes.purpose: Get out before the doors close.
sceneTypes.tips: If the alarm is high the building is hunting you: the scene becomes a chase. Otherwise you slip away and describe it.

setup.title: How hot is it out there?
setup.tip: Decided by the alarm: above 3 and you are chased.

sceneTypes.name: Chase
sceneTypes.purpose: Lose the pursuit on the streets.
sceneTypes.tips: Describe streets, traffic and the vehicles behind you. Use the Fate question to see if you lose them, and your Cyberpunk RED rules for the driving (see the Cyberpunk RED core rulebook, Combat chapter).

setup.title: Who takes the wheel?
setup.tip: A nomad in the crew is a good choice.

play.title: Do you lose them?
play.tip: Roll Cool and set the difficulty from how good the pursuers are.

play.title: Boxed in
play.prompt: They box you in. You get away, but the score stays behind.

play.title: Shaken, not caught
play.prompt: Shaking them costs you. What do you leave behind?

sceneTypes.name: Payday
sceneTypes.purpose: Get paid, or not.
sceneTypes.tips: Without the objective there is no pay. With it, the client pays what was promised and you check if they keep their word.

setup.title: No job, no pay.
setup.tip: Say what it costs you, and who you owe now.

setup.title: The client pays up.
setup.prompt: The client pays {fact:payout}. Was the job worth it?

setup.title: Is it a double-cross?
setup.tip: Roll 1d6. A 1 means the client sells you out.

sceneTypes.name: Edgerunner
sceneTypes.purpose: Make the character you will play.
sceneTypes.tips: Start with a street name and a role. You can edit the sheet any time in the Characters panel. You begin with 500 eb and an empty kit: the Night Market sells the rest.

setup.title: Who are you?
setup.tip: Make your character: a street name, a role, a few stats and your kit.

sceneTypes.name: Turf
sceneTypes.purpose: Claim your corner of the city and name your crew.
sceneTypes.tips: Think small: a block, a bar, a stairwell. Where you start shapes every gig that follows.

setup.title: Which block is your turf?
setup.tip: A district, a street or a building. Write what makes it yours.

setup.title: What do you call your crew?
setup.tip: Even a crew of one needs a name people can whisper.

sceneTypes.name: Fixer
sceneTypes.purpose: Meet the person who brings you work.
sceneTypes.tips: A fixer wants a cut and a favor. Decide what yours is hiding.

setup.title: Who is your fixer?
setup.tip: Just a street name: it becomes the NPC's name. Write what they want from you in a note.

sceneTypes.name: Gig offer
sceneTypes.purpose: Hear a job offer and decide whether to take it.
sceneTypes.tips: Who is asking, what do they want and what are they not saying? Taking the gig starts a chain: legwork, the job, then payday. The alarm starts at zero for every gig.

setup.title: Who offers the gig?
setup.tip: Just a street name: it becomes the NPC's name. Skip it if the fixer is the one asking.

setup.title: What is the gig?
setup.tip: One sentence: what they want done, and what they are not saying.

closing.title: Take it?
closing.tip: Yes starts the gig with some legwork. No leaves the offer behind.

sceneTypes.name: Legwork
sceneTypes.purpose: Learn what you need before the gig goes loud.
sceneTypes.tips: Scout, ask around, call in a favor. Each scene should give you one useful fact. When you know enough, go.

closing.title: Did you gain an edge?
closing.tip: Choose Yes if the legwork taught you something that will help on the job.

sceneTypes.name: Job
sceneTypes.purpose: Do the gig in one scene.
sceneTypes.tips: A short heist: one question, the trouble that follows and how it ends. Mistakes raise the alarm. A spare edge can clean up after you.

play.title: Does it go to plan?
play.tip: A yes skips the trouble. A no raises the alarm by one, an exceptional no by two.

play.title: What goes wrong?
play.tip: Some entries move the alarm for you.

closing.title: Spend an edge to clean up?
closing.tip: Spending it costs one edge and lowers the alarm by one.

sceneTypes.name: Gig payday
sceneTypes.purpose: Get paid and count what the gig did to your name.
sceneTypes.tips: A clean job earns more rep. The pay grows with your rep, so a good name pays for itself. Any loose end can come back later.

setup.title: How clean was it?
setup.tip: Decided by the alarm: 3 or less earns 2 rep, more earns 1.

play.title: Collect the pay
play.tip: Choose your Character: the pay is 200 eb plus 50 eb for each point of rep.

closing.title: Any loose ends?
closing.tip: A witness, a debt, a client who knows too much. Each answer becomes a Thread.

sceneTypes.name: Downtime
sceneTypes.purpose: Rest, recover and let the month pass.
sceneTypes.tips: Say how the crew spends its days. Each Downtime is one more week on the Month clock: at 4/4 the rent is due. The Night Market stalls and finds tables are there if you want ideas.

play.title: How do you spend the downtime?

closing.title: A week slips by. What changed?
closing.tip: Answering moves the Month clock by one.

closing.title: Hit the Night Market?
closing.tip: Yes visits the Night Market before the rent comes due.

sceneTypes.name: Recruit
sceneTypes.purpose: Find someone to join the crew.
sceneTypes.tips: A crew of two or more is how you get ready to go big. Say who they are, what they want and what they do best.

setup.title: Who joins?
setup.tip: Just a street name: it becomes the NPC's name.

setup.title: What do they do best?
setup.tip: Their specialty becomes a tag on the NPC.

sceneTypes.name: Hit squad
sceneTypes.purpose: Survive the people sent to shut you up.
sceneTypes.tips: Too much heat brings professionals. Keep it fast and mean. When it is over, the heat drops, but the people who sent them remember.

setup.title: Who sent them, and how do they find you?

closing.title: How do you get clear?
closing.tip: Answering lowers the heat to 4 and drops any gig.

sceneTypes.name: Gear up
sceneTypes.purpose: Get what the big job needs.
sceneTypes.tips: Decide what is missing from the plan, and who has it. The Night Market sells gear, food and chrome for eddies.

play.title: What do you need, and who has it?

sceneTypes.name: Night Market
sceneTypes.purpose: Buy and sell gear, food and chrome.
sceneTypes.tips: A few stalls are open tonight. Choose your Character, sell what you do not need and buy what you do. Prices come from the catalog; chrome goes in the Cyberware inventory.

setup.title: What does the market look like tonight?

play.title: What do you buy or sell?
play.prompt: A few stalls are open tonight.

sceneTypes.name: Month's end
sceneTypes.purpose: Pay the rent, eat what you can afford and think about moving up.
sceneTypes.tips: Rent depends on where you live. If you cannot pay, skip it: your lifestyle drops and a fixer holds the debt. Either way the Month clock starts again.

play.title: Pay the rent (500 eb)?
play.tip: Choose your Character. Skipping costs a step of lifestyle and a debt.

play.title: Pay the rent (1,000 eb)?
play.tip: Choose your Character. Skipping costs a step of lifestyle and a debt.

play.title: Pay the rent (1,500 eb)?
play.tip: Choose your Character. Skipping costs a step of lifestyle and a debt.

play.title: Pay the rent (2,500 eb)?
play.tip: Choose your Character. Skipping costs a step of lifestyle and a debt.

play.title: Which fixer do you borrow from?
Eat better (300 eb)?
play.tip: Choose your Character. Yes raises your lifestyle by one.

play.title: Move up?
play.tip: Yes upgrades your housing for next month.

sceneTypes.name: Fallout
sceneTypes.purpose: Count what the big job gave you and what it cost.
sceneTypes.tips: With the score in hand your rep soars. Without it the heat does. Either way someone knows it was you.

play.title: Collect the score
play.tip: Choose your Character: the score pays 1,000 eb plus 100 eb for each point of rep.

closing.title: Who knows it was you?
closing.tip: Each answer becomes a Thread that can come back.

sceneTypes.name: Betrayal
sceneTypes.purpose: Find out who sold you out.
sceneTypes.tips: The twist is that someone you trusted was playing a longer game. A fixer is the first suspect, then a client. If you have neither, decide for yourself.

setup.title: Did your fixer sell you out?
Did a client sell you out?
Who sold you out?
setup.tip: Nobody on your lists fits, so decide who it was.

setup.title: What is the twist?
setup.tip: If someone was picked, {picked} sold you to {fact:nemesis}. Make the roll yours.

sceneTypes.name: Showdown
sceneTypes.purpose: Face your nemesis.
sceneTypes.tips: Everything you built is in this scene: crew, gear, rep and the people you wronged. Run the fight with your Cyberpunk RED rules (see the Cyberpunk RED core rulebook, Combat chapter) and use this scene for the story.

play.title: Where do you face your nemesis?
play.tip: Your nemesis: {fact:nemesis}. If the slot is empty, decide who it is now.

play.title: Does it go your way?
play.tip: Ask as likely if the crew is strong and unlikely if you are alone.

play.title: What does winning, or losing, cost?

sceneTypes.name: Epilogue
sceneTypes.purpose: Say how it ends.
sceneTypes.tips: Look back on the three acts. When you finish this scene the guided flow is done and you can keep playing freely.

setup.title: Was the big job worth it?
setup.tip: The big job: {fact:big-job}.

setup.title: Where does the crew stand now?
setup.tip: {fact:crew-name}: rep {tracker:rep}, heat {tracker:heat}.

flows.name: Heist
flows.description: A one-shot heist for one sitting: set it up, do the legwork, pull the job, get away.
flows.introduction:
Solo play means you are the whole table: you describe what happens, roll the dice and make the calls. This guide gives you the questions so you can keep the story moving.

You play one job: you put a crew together, meet the client, scout the place, pull the heist, get away and get paid. Each step asks you something or tells you what to roll. Steps marked mandatory must be done; the others are suggested and you can skip them.

Watch the Alarm clock. Mistakes and bad luck fill it. When it reaches 6 the building locks down and the job is over: you run.

In the legwork and the heist you choose which scene to play next. When you are ready to leave a phase, use End the phase. Rules for fighting, hacking and skills come from your Cyberpunk RED book: this guide only decides what happens next.

sceneClosing.title: Did you gain an edge?
sceneClosing.tip: Choose Yes if the scene taught you something that will help in the heist.

worldTurn.title: Does word get around?
worldTurn.tip: Roll 1d6. A 1 raises the alarm by one before the heist even starts.

sceneOpening.title: Security is on alert
sceneOpening.prompt: The alarm is at {tracker:alarm}. What do you notice?
sceneOpening.tip: Guards are tense and doors are watched. Let it shape the scene.

sceneClosing.title: Spend an edge to avoid trouble?
sceneClosing.tip: Spending it skips the complication and costs one edge.

sceneClosing.title: What goes wrong?
sceneClosing.tip: Some entries move the alarm for you.

worldTurn.title: Do the guards find you?
worldTurn.tip: Roll 1d6. On 1 to 3 a firefight starts right now.

flows.name: Making a Name
flows.description: A campaign in three acts: make a name on the street with gigs, pull the big job, then face the twist.
flows.introduction:
Solo play means you are the whole table: you describe what happens, roll the dice and make the calls. This guide gives you the questions so you can keep the story moving.

You play a campaign in three acts. In Act 1 you make a name: take gigs from your fixer, grow your rep, recruit a crew and spend your downtime. Rep opens doors. Heat closes them: at 8 or more someone sends a hit squad. In Act 2 you plan and pull the big job. In Act 3 the twist arrives: someone you trusted sold you out, and you face your nemesis.

Between gigs you live on eddies. Every four Downtime scenes the month ends: pay the rent or take the debt, eat better if you can and move up if you dare. Spend your eddies at the Night Market on gear, food and chrome.

Each step asks you something or tells you what to roll. Steps marked mandatory must be done; the others are suggested and you can skip them. Rules for fighting, hacking and skills come from your Cyberpunk RED book: this guide only decides what happens next.

phases.name: Street zero
phases.description: Make your character, claim your turf and meet your fixer. Done when the fixer scene ends.

phases.name: Making a name
phases.description: Take gigs, recruit a crew and spend your downtime. Done when your rep is 5 or more, you have two crew and you choose to go big, or when you move on.

sceneClosing.title: Is a gig running?
sceneClosing.tip: While a gig runs the street waits and Act 1 cannot end.

sceneClosing.title: Go big?
sceneClosing.tip: Your name is out there and you have a crew. Yes ends Act 1 and starts planning the big job.

worldTurn.title: Is a gig running?
worldTurn.tip: While a gig runs the street waits.

worldTurn.title: Does the street stir?
worldTurn.tip: Roll 1d6. On 5 or 6 something happens in the streets.

worldTurn.title: What is the rival crew after?
Who holds a grudge against you?
worldTurn.tip: Just a street name: it becomes the NPC and your nemesis.

worldTurn.title: Is the heat too high?
worldTurn.tip: At 8 or more a hit squad comes.

phases.name: Planning
phases.description: Scout the big job, recruit and gear up. Done when you move on to the job.

phaseOpening.title: Act 2: The big job. What is it?
phaseOpening.tip: One sentence: the target, and why it is worth everything you built.

phases.name: The job
phases.description: Pull the big job. Done when you grab the score or the alarm is full.

sceneOpening.title: Security is on alert
sceneOpening.prompt: The alarm is at {tracker:alarm}. What do you notice?
sceneOpening.tip: Guards are tense and doors are watched. Let it shape the scene.

sceneClosing.title: Spend an edge to avoid trouble?
sceneClosing.tip: Spending it skips the complication and costs one edge.

sceneClosing.title: What goes wrong?
sceneClosing.tip: Some entries move the alarm for you.

worldTurn.title: Do the guards close in?
worldTurn.tip: Roll 1d6. On 1 or 2 the alarm rises by one.

phases.name: Fallout
phases.description: Get away, then count the cost. Done when the fallout scene ends.

phases.name: Finale
phases.description: Learn who sold you out, face your nemesis and say how it ends.

fields.label: Role
fields.hint: Your trade on a job: what the crew calls you for.

fields.label: Nerve
fields.hint: Staying cool when it goes wrong.

fields.label: Hands
fields.hint: Quick, careful work: locks, wires, triggers.

fields.label: Wits
fields.hint: Reading a room and a plan.

fields.label: Grit
fields.hint: Taking a hit and staying on your feet.

fields.label: Cool
fields.hint: Nerve, minus half the Alarm: how steady you stay as security closes in.

fields.label: HP
fields.hint: Hit points: at zero you are down.

fields.label: Wounded at
fields.hint: Half your HP: at or below it you are badly hurt.

fields.label: Humanity
fields.hint: What is left of you under the chrome.

fields.label: Eddies
fields.hint: Your money. Gigs pay it, rent and shops take it.

checks.label: Nerve check
checks.hint: Stay steady when the job goes wrong.

checks.label: Hands check
checks.hint: Quick, careful work: a lock, a wire, a trigger.

checks.label: Wits check
checks.hint: Read the room, spot the flaw in the plan.

checks.label: Grit check
checks.hint: Take the hit and stay on your feet.

checks.label: Cool check
checks.hint: Keep your head while security closes in.

gear.name: Used pistol
gear.description: Reliable enough, and nobody asks where it came from.

gear.name: Armor jacket
gear.description: Light armor that passes for street wear.

gear.name: Burner agent
gear.description: A cheap agent you throw away after one job.

gear.name: Climbing gear

gear.name: Medkit
gear.description: Patches you up enough to keep walking.

gear.name: Real coffee
gear.description: A luxury that tastes like the old days.

gear.name: Cheap cyberoptic
gear.description: A mass-market eye with a few tricks.

gear.name: Neural link
gear.description: The port every netrunner starts from.
